holidays.name: St. Patrick's Day
holidays.description: A day when the whole world pretends to be Irish, wears green to avoid being pinched, and drinks plenty of green beer. Cities from Chicago to Savannah go all out with parades, shamrocks, and leprechaun-themed everything.
holidays.origin: It began as a feast day marking the death of St. Patrick, the 5th-century patron saint of Ireland, who is traditionally said to have used the three-leaf shamrock to explain the Holy Trinity. Irish immigrants in America turned it into a big cultural celebration.
holidays.funFact: Chicago has dyed its river bright green every year since 1962, using about 40 pounds of vegetable-based dye. The first St. Patrick's Day parade was held in the American colonies, not in Ireland, in the 1600s or 1700s.

holidays.name: Submarine Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the underwater vessels that quietly lurk beneath the waves. It also doubles as a nod to the sandwich of the same name, so some people celebrate with a sub in hand.
holidays.origin: The date commemorates the 1898 launch of the USS Holland, the first submarine commissioned by the U.S. Navy, designed by Irish-American inventor John Philip Holland. The Navy later made it an unofficial annual tribute to submariners.
holidays.funFact: John Philip Holland was born in Ireland, which makes the date a fitting overlap with St. Patrick's Day.

holidays.name: Awareness Day for Corned Beef and Cabbage
holidays.description: A celebration of the salty, tender meal that many people eat on St. Patrick's Day, even though it is more of an Irish-American tradition than an Irish one.
holidays.origin: Irish immigrants in the United States in the 1800s swapped expensive Irish bacon for cheaper corned beef from their Jewish neighbors in New York's Lower East Side. Cabbage was a cheap and easy side.
holidays.funFact: Americans consume an estimated 26 million pounds of corned beef around St. Patrick's Day, and in Ireland the traditional meal was actually boiled bacon and cabbage.

holidays.name: World Sleep Day (Friday before the March equinox)
holidays.description: A day devoted to appreciating the value of a good night's sleep, with events that encourage better rest habits. Nap enthusiasts consider it a holy day.
holidays.origin: Created by the World Sleep Society's World Sleep Day Committee in 2008 to raise awareness of sleep problems and promote healthy sleep. It is held on a Friday in mid-March and sometimes lands on March 17.
holidays.funFact: Humans spend about a third of their lives asleep, which adds up to around 26 years for someone who lives to 80.

holidays.name: Lag BaOmer-style Corned Beef... Oops, Let's Go With Quirky: National Quirky Dance Day Not Official, So Try Kick Dance Day
holidays.description: An unofficial day when people embrace goofy dancing, which often happens spontaneously at St. Patrick's Day gatherings and the jigs that come with them.
holidays.origin: It grew informally from the lively tradition of Irish step dancing, which gained huge worldwide popularity after Riverdance debuted in 1994.
holidays.funFact: The original Riverdance performance was a seven-minute interval act at the 1994 Eurovision Song Contest, and it got such a huge response that it became a full-length stage show.
